summary: V1 (structure-only applicability, now including identity keys) and V2 (JSON-only profile review) are fixed. Both refuse before any read and hold against my adversarial fixtures. The worker's only edit to my test file was removing the three strict-xfail decorators. No residuals.

checks.evidence: tests/test_release_builder_gaps_verify.py has no xfail markers left (the docstring mention aside). The bodies of test_structural_only_applicability_is_refused (its parametrize kept) and test_non_json_profile_review_values_fail_with_a_release_error match what I wrote. The builder sha256 equals the handoff value.

_TASK_KEYS = {task, task_id, observation_type} plus IDENTITY_COLUMNS. For both reviewed and approved profiles, each of these is refused before any read (zero pq.read_table calls), with no bundle: {subject}, {source_recording_id}, {observation_id}, {task, observation_type, reference_side} and {subject, task_id}. {population, reference_side, observation_type} still releases and filters (1 observation passes). Unknown or mis-cased keys cannot pass anything: they match no metadata and leave observations unchecked, so they fail safe. Legacy profiles without a status are not subject to the rule, by design, and keep their limitation.

These are refused before any read with 'JSON values', for legacy profiles too: a scalar YAML date review, a nested unquoted date, .nan, .inf, a !!set and a !!binary value. For reviewed profiles, the unquoted-date case (my former CORE-09-V2 xfail) is now a ReleaseError. An unquoted date outside the review (top-level 'generated') does not block the release and does not reach manifest.profile, because only the review is copied into the JSON outputs.

The release-section sentence names task, task_id, observation_type and the identity columns as insufficient alone, and says any profile whose review holds a non-JSON value is refused. Both match the code.
